mechanism.owner_quote: Sharding is an application-level routing contract: a versioned shard map assigns each key to a shard, the request carries the shard key, and the store enforces one owner per key.

invariant.owner_quote: One authoritative owner must exist per key, and a resharding move must fence writes or preserve a verifiable handoff.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Hotspots, map drift, split brain and a failed migration are common; detect skew, throttle the hot key and dual-read/verify during movement.

alternative.owner_quote: Partitioning inside one database, read replicas or vertical scaling may be preferable when distribution would add cross-shard coordination without relieving the measured constraint.

mechanism.owner_quote: Partitioning splits one logical data set into key ranges or lists inside a store so the planner can prune unrelated partitions for a query.
mechanism.reason: Defines key-range or list splits for planner pruning.

invariant.owner_quote: Each row belongs to exactly one partition, and the main query must name a partition key so pruning is possible.
invariant.reason: Requires one partition per row and a named partition key for pruning.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A query without the partition key fans out across every partition; inspect plans and measure fan-out when access paths or keys change.
failure_recovery.reason: Names fan-out without the key and requires plan and fan-out checks.

alternative.owner_quote: Keep one table and add an index when the main query already prunes; partition only when the data volume, retention or maintenance benefit is measured.
alternative.reason: Contrasts one indexed table with measured partitioning benefit.

mechanism.owner_quote: Consistent hashing maps keys onto a ring so adding or removing a node moves only the adjacent share of keys instead of remapping the whole keyspace.
mechanism.reason: Defines ring placement with only adjacent key movement.

invariant.owner_quote: Clients and owners must agree on a versioned mapping, and a key must retain one authoritative owner at any mapping epoch.
invariant.reason: Requires a versioned mapping and one authoritative owner per epoch.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A ring change temporarily routes a key to the wrong owner or serves an incomplete copy; dual-read or version-check during the transition and record the epoch.
failure_recovery.reason: Names wrong-owner or incomplete-copy transitions and requires dual-read or version checks.

alternative.owner_quote: Explicit key-range assignment gives direct control of hot ranges; choose consistent hashing when node membership changes often and manual range planning is impractical.
alternative.reason: Contrasts explicit key-range assignment for hot ranges.

sections: 26.2.3. Preparing the Primary for Standby Servers

mechanism.owner_quote: One leader accepts writes and appends a replicated log; followers apply it in order.

invariant.owner_quote: A stale leader can remain reachable to some clients, but must not be allowed to commit new authoritative writes without a valid quorum/term contract.
invariant.reason: States the single-writer rule during a partition.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Promotion requires a quorum/term check and a fencing token; the old leader must be rejected, and the follower log must catch up before it serves authoritative reads.
failure_recovery.reason: Covers isolation, new-leader election and stale-leader rejection with log catch-up.

alternative.owner_quote: Quorum-replicated consensus, multi-leader replication or asynchronous read replicas may be preferable depending on the required write availability, read freshness and conflict model.

mechanism.owner_quote: Several nodes accept writes for the same logical data and replicate them to each other, so every accepted write must eventually converge to one declared outcome.
mechanism.reason: Defines multiple write acceptors with eventual convergence.

invariant.owner_quote: The system must define a conflict-resolution rule and preserve every acknowledged effect according to that rule; silent last-writer-wins is not a convergence proof.
invariant.reason: Requires a conflict rule and preservation of every acknowledged effect.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Concurrent writes to one key produce conflicts that surface later during reads or reconciliation; record the conflicting versions and expose a deterministic resolution path.
failure_recovery.reason: Requires recording conflicting versions and a deterministic resolution path.

alternative.owner_quote: Single-leader replication avoids write conflicts at the cost of write availability across regions; choose multi-leader only when accepting local writes outweighs the conflict contract.
alternative.reason: Contrasts single-leader conflict avoidance with write availability.

sections: 26.2.3. Preparing the Primary for Standby Servers

mechanism.owner_quote: Read replicas serve read-only traffic from followers, reducing load on the leader while accepting that a replica can lag behind the latest committed write.
mechanism.reason: Defines follower read serving with bounded lag.

invariant.owner_quote: A read must state the freshness it requires, and read-your-writes or monotonic guarantees must be enforced by routing, a position wait or an authority read.
invariant.reason: Requires a freshness statement and routing, wait or authority read for stronger guarantees.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A lag spike serves stale data even though replication is healthy; monitor applied position and lag, and route freshness-critical reads away from a lagging replica.
failure_recovery.reason: Requires applied-position and lag monitoring with freshness-critical routing.

alternative.owner_quote: Read from the leader or use a quorum read when freshness dominates; add replicas when read volume and tolerance for bounded staleness justify the extra copies.
alternative.reason: Names leader or quorum reads when freshness dominates.

mechanism.owner_quote: Let N be the replica count, W the acknowledgements required for a write and R the responses required for a read.

invariant.owner_quote: During a membership change, require the old and new quorums to overlap

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Overlap is necessary but not sufficient for freshness: choose the response with the highest version and repair replicas behind it.
failure_recovery.reason: Names stale-read failure and version/read-repair recovery.

alternative.owner_quote: Use this when the chosen W/R latency fits and the membership service is trustworthy.

mechanism.owner_quote: An index table is an application-owned lookup table that maps a query key to a primary key or row locator.

invariant.owner_quote: Every lookup row must resolve to the current base row

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Dual-write ambiguity, partial backfill, duplicate lookup keys and stale rows are common design-time failure modes

alternative.owner_quote: A native secondary index, a materialized view or a query-time join may be preferable when the primary store already serves the access path.

mechanism.owner_quote: A single authoritative registration database plus a graph/search/OLAP projection is a valid possible design—but then there are *two data representations*, not two automatically consistent sources of truth.
mechanism.reason: Describes the multi-store design and its duplicate representation.

invariant.owner_quote: Define freshness, rebuild, deduplication, schema migration and failure recovery explicitly.
invariant.reason: States the required freshness, rebuild and recovery contract.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Dual-write ambiguity and partial migration need an explicit reconciliation owner; a half-migrated projection is not a valid serving state.
failure_recovery.reason: Names dual-write ambiguity and partial migration with a reconciliation owner, not a freshness contract.

alternative.owner_quote: A single store with derived projections or query-time joins may be preferable when one engine can meet the query shapes and the team cannot operate a second consistency contract.
alternative.reason: Names the single-store alternative and reversal.

mechanism.owner_quote: The projection owner publishes the event schema it accepts, the position it has applied and the staleness callers should expect.
mechanism.reason: Bounded owner statement from the current section.

invariant.owner_quote: Those commitments belong in the read contract, not in an operator's memory.
invariant.reason: Bounded owner statement from the current section.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Apply events idempotently and reject a position that would move the projection backwards; a duplicate must not create a second effect.
failure_recovery.reason: Bounded owner statement from the current section.

alternative.owner_quote: An authority read or simpler cache may serve the journey with fewer contracts
alternative.reason: Bounded owner statement from the current section.
